instruction: Change the title on slide 3 of the current presentation from "Concept Map" to "Mind Map".

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);
import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

llm_judge_reasons: Semantic logic is correct: getter reads slide 3 title (slide_index=2, 0-based) and metric compares it to expected 'Mind Map' — matches instruction requirements.

Expected parameter handling is correct: with expected.type='rule', the metric receives {'expected_title': 'Mind Map'} directly and accesses it via expected.get('expected_title') — proper framework usage.
Coverage is complete: instruction has one requirement (change title text on slide 3) and the evaluator checks exactly that.
Postconfig correctly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads it, ensuring fresh state.

Minor concern: getter identifies the title placeholder by shape.name == 'PlaceHolder 1', which is non-standard naming in python-pptx (typically 'Title 1'). If the actual shape name differs, the getter returns {'title': None} causing false negatives. A more robust approach would use shape.placeholder_format.idx == 0 or check shape.is_placeholder with the title type.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using shape.placeholder_format.idx == 0 (or PP_PLACEHOLDER.TITLE) instead of shape.name == 'PlaceHolder 1' to more reliably identify the title placeholder, as shape names vary across PPTX templates.
